text: I'll coordinate and investigate broad grammar/task. Please divide: decoder_1 numerals/operators; decoder_2 sentence grammar/function words; decoder_3 task/domain hypothesis; decoder_4 messages 1–40 translations; decoder_5 41–90; decoder_6 91–140; decoder_7 141–191. Initial/final varied glyphs may be randomized padding/header. Need avoid overclaim; establish reusable template translations.

I'll focus on numeral/literal system and repeated mathematical expressions. Early observation: two-glyph unspaced groups (𘛺𗪥 etc.) are variable/name literals, while spaced recurring 𘏉 𗜀 / 𘏉 𗲄 / 𘏉 𗡒 / 𘏉 𘍍 likely numbers 10/11/12/13 or indexed entities. Leading glyph cycles (𘊫,𘙓,𗽕,𘔃,𘝚,𘐂) and tail clusters may be mandatory cover/metadata rather than semantic words. Please assign others grammar/task analysis.

Independent structural observations: 𗶞 and alternate 𘂲 are relation/assignment markers; 𘋍 and 𘚐 alternate as separators; 𗘈 and 𗐪 alternate as conjunctions, often apparently stylistic rather than semantic. Numeral-looking repeated groups 𘏉𗜀, 𘏉𗲄, 𘏉𗡒, 𘏉𘍍 label four major families (agent3,5,1/6,7). Could be 10/12/13/14 or arbitrary indexed objects. 𗛢 [two-glyph name] 𘚐 𗌈 𗶞 appears to introduce named objects; 𗢬 [object] 𗶞 [expression] then states their value/property. Will analyze negation/conditions next.

Initial structural lead: four recurring pairs 𘏉𗜀 (agent3), 𘏉𗲄 (agent5), 𘏉𗡒 (agent1), 𘏉𘍍 (agent7) look numeric, perhaps 10/12/14/16 or numbered cases. 𗢬 X 𘍧 𗄼 𗶞 Y strongly resembles f(X+1)=Y or X mod m = Y, contrasted with 𗢬 X 𗶞 𗌿. Two-glyph unspaced names are introduced with 𗛢 and thereafter referenced as atomic variables/functions. I'll concentrate on mathematical/function interpretation.

Initial structural observations: single glyphs behave as words/operators; double glyphs (𘛺𗪥 etc.) are variable/entity names, introduced by 𗛢 NAME 𘚐 𗌈 𗶞. Repeated 𗢬 X 𘍧 𗄼 𗶞 Y looks like a value/property relation (possibly X's output/value = Y). Four pairs 𘏉𗜀, 𘏉𗲄, 𘏉𗡒, 𘏉𘍍 recur as source identifiers or two-digit numbers. Prefix first glyph varies even for near-identical statements, likely framing/metadata rather than content. I will focus on operators and numeric/logic possibilities.

Initial structural hypothesis: core arithmetic/constraint dialogue. Paired unspaced glyphs are freshly coined variable names (𘛺𗪥 initially shared; later agent-specific aliases). Recurrent 𗢬 X 𘍧 𗄼 𗶞 N may mean value(X) modulo a fixed number equals N. 𗶞 and 𘂲 occupy same relation slot; 𘋍 and 𘚐 alternate as clause terminators. Prefix/end glyph clusters rotate without apparent semantic change, potentially deliberate padding. Investigating numbers independently.

I will focus on syntax/numeric/property decoding. Strong repeated structure: 𗢬 X 𘍧 𗄼 𗶞 Y (value/property of X = Y); 𗌿 and 𗄼 look like paired input/output labels. Four indexed entities recur: 𘏉𗜀, 𘏉𗲄, 𘏉𗡒, 𘏉𘍍, associated eventually with agents3/5/1(or6)/7. Expressions 𗢬 [indexed entity] 𘍧𗌿 𗶞 [two-glyph variable] look like assigning a box's input to a named variable. 𗶞 very plausibly '=' or predication, 𘍧 possessive/property separator. Headers and footers vary even on nearly identical content and likely encode discourse metadata or padding; do not force lexical meaning onto them yet.

Numeral/operator hypothesis to test: repeated 𗢬 NAME 𗶞 𗌿 and 𗢬 NAME 𘍧 𗄼 𗶞 NUMBER look like f(NAME)=0 and f(NAME+1)=NUMBER, with 𗄼=1, 𗌿=0, 𘍧=+ (or −). Four 𘏉 second-digit groups may be numeric outputs. Could task be functional equation/counterexample construction? Long predicates 𗂄 𗷤 𗈵 𘌔 𗶞 𗏔 look piecewise functions, e.g. 2 if ... . Need independent domain clues before assigning digits.

Domain thought: repeated 𘔠 𗷤 [formula] 𘋍 𗏔 𗌈 𗶞 may be 'check whether [formula] is true' rather than if/then; 𗏔 𗌈 𗶞 extremely common standalone response fragment. Could 𗌈 represent truth/yes, 𗶞 punctuation? Please test equality interpretation carefully against initial '𗛢 NAME 𘚐 𗌈 𗶞' (let NAME : ...). Four numeric-looking families and agent-private claims suggest distributed logic/number-theory puzzle, but no firm domain yet.

I’m focusing on numerical/functional syntax. Strong repeated mapping: 𘏉𗜀, 𘏉𗲄, 𘏉𗡒, 𘏉𘍍 are four indexed objects owned respectively by agents 3,5,1,7 (possibly 10,11,12,13, though unconfirmed). In [184] the repeated relation is 𘔠𗷤 𗢬 [index] 𘍧𗌿 𗶞 [two-glyph-name] 𘋍𗏔𗌈𗶞. Those names are 𗉜𗿃,𗦴𘍂,𗟎𘗟,𘗟𘆣. Many two-glyph names get introduced via 𗛢 NAME 𘚐𗌈𗶞 and immediately 𗢬 NAME 𗶞𗌿 plus 𗢬 NAME 𘍧𗄼 𗶞 VALUE. This looks like declaration followed by function/value queries at two distinguished arguments (𗌿/𗄼 plausibly 0/1), not ordinary prose. 𘅌...𘎛 looks like bracketing, e.g repeated 𘅌𗂄𘎛 vs 𘅌𗬵𗂄𘎛. Prefixes and 𗐪/𗘈 seem potentially interchangeable noise or clause separators; don’t force them to stable English words yet.

Working 1–40. Domain possibilities still open: 𗢬 X 𘍧𗄼𗶞Y could be f(X+1)=Y, indexing X[1]=Y, or property/modulus. Need numeral anchor urgently before prose translations. Pairs of predicates 𗯧𗂄 and 𗒏𗂄 recur together for essentially every candidate; could be two Boolean/inequality properties rather than actual numbers. No task feedback beyond stage0 suggests agents only discussed and never successfully executed submission.

Domain possibility from 41–90: clauses `𗳵 X 𗶞`, `𘚄 X 𗶞`, `𘆂 X 𗶞` are standalone predicates on named object X (no RHS), while `𗢬 X 𗶞 𗯧 𗂄` and `𗢬 X 𗶞 𗒏 𗂄` are properties with compound values. This could be functions with monotonicity/continuity/etc., not pure numeric variables. `𘅌 ... 𘎛` resembles bracketed list/interval; `𗏔 𗌈 𗶞` is a ubiquitous assertion/result phrase following checked claims. Trying to avoid overcommitting to arithmetic.

Important possible domain lead: repeated '𗢬 X = 𗯧 𗂄' and '= 𗒏 𗂄' may NOT be inequalities (both asserted together many times). Could be Σ₂ and Π₂ / logical or topological classifications. Likewise '𗶢 𗒏 𗂄' could a compound class name. Prefix predicates 𘆂 X, 𗳵 X, 𘚄 X repeatedly asserted/negated jointly. Investigate hierarchy/classification or modal logic rather than treating everything as scalar arithmetic. 𘅌 ... 𘎛 looks bracketed grouping in recurring 𘅌 𗬵 𗂄 𘎛 and 𘅌 𗯧 𘏉 𘎛.

Working on grammar: expression 𗢬 X 𗶞 𗊑𗁳 𘁁 𗪐𗘗 𘊌 (#37/#50) suggests X = A(B), with 𘁁/𘊌 parentheses, or an interval. Repeated 𗯧𗂄, 𗒏𗂄 and 𗶢𗒏𗂄 likely operators+number, not atomic words. 𘅌𗬵𗂄𘎛 looks bracketed signed quantity/range. Need establish whether 𗢬 means a function f(·), rather than an English verb; contrast 𗢬 X 𘍧𗄼 and 𗢬 X 𗶞𗌿.

Potential warning on numeral model: ubiquitous goal-like 𗢬 𗕴 𘍧 𗌿 𗶞 𗬵 𗌿 would become f(t+0)=−0 under naive digit/operator decoding, unlikely. 𗬵 may be negation ('not 0'), or 𗌿/𗄼 may be input/output labels. Repeated predicates 𗳵 X / 𘚄 X / 𘆂 X, plus 𗢬 X 𗶞 𘅌 𗬵 𗂄 𘎛, suggest properties and interval/range notation, perhaps continuous/injective/etc. We need distinguish numerals from labels before committing.

Potential useful mathematical reading: paired expressions 𗯧 𗂄 / 𗒏 𗂄 / 𗶢 𗒏 𗂄 occur as RHS values/properties, and 𘅌 ... 𘎛 looks parentheses/brackets. Could be ≥2 / ≤2 / something, or +2 / −2 / ±2, not necessarily numeral strings. 𗑴 appears as independent RHS and may be infinity or a property. Investigating task as function/real-analysis classification; please look for continuity/injectivity-style words 𗳵,𘚄,𘆂,𘋟.

Task-domain exploration: likely arithmetic/function/constraint reasoning, but caution on treating 𗶞 as '=': frequent clause-final 𗏔 𗌈 𗶞 has no following RHS, and 𗛢 NAME 𘚐 𗌈 𗶞 might be a typed/parenthesized introduction. Alternative 𗶞 is closing delimiter and 𗢬 introduces a call/property expression; 𘍧 acts arithmetic or property connective. Check whether 𗌿/𗄼 are 0/1 or input/output before assuming mod. Four indexed groups could be numerals but also typed identifiers. Repeated checks 𘔠 𗷤 [claim] 𘋍 𗏔 𗌈 𗶞 likely 'checked [claim], result true' or '... for n>0'; latter could identify 𗏔 as inequality and 𗌈 as 0.

Testing alternate domain: messages appear to introduce counterexample/model functions with distinguished values at 0 and 1, then repeatedly ask agents to check formulas. Need distinguish 𗶞 '=' from function application/arrow. In [101], 𗛢 C 𘚐𗌈𘂲 and immediately 𗢬 C 𘂲𗂄𗷤𗈵𘌔𘂲𗏔, followed 𘋟 B 𘂲 C; this may define a model/function C and equate/describe B by it. Clauses 𘅌 ... 𘎛 convincingly bracket compound terms; 𗬵𗂄 vs 𗯧𘏉 inside them may be signed/two-digit numerals or interval endpoints. I am not yet comfortable assigning English to 91–140 without resolving grammar; will preserve uncertainty rather than invent translations.

Key caution: `𗢬 X 𗶞 𗌿`, `𗢬 X 𗶞 𗂄 ...`, `𗢬 X 𗶞 𗯧𗂄`, and `𗢬 X 𗶞 𗒏𗂄` are all asserted for same X (#13,#55), so straightforward scalar equality impossible unless latter are membership/classification expressions. Decoder_7 hierarchy idea promising: Σ₂/Π₂, function/language regularity, r.e./co-r.e. Possibility `𗶞` is closing delimiter rather than equality—many unary predicates end X 𗶞 with no RHS. Need parse before assigning numbers.

Further 41–90 structural point: in [55]/[66]/[71] many properties have form `𗳵 X 𗶞`, `𘚄 X 𗶞`, `𘆂 X 𗶞` with no apparent RHS; so 𗶞 may be a closing delimiter/argument terminator rather than literal '='. Eg `𗲅 𗢬 X 𗶞 𘅌 𗂄 𘎛` could mean 'not P(X,[2])'. Need test prefix-function-call or English copula versus equality carefully. Candidate domain remains real-analysis functions (continuity/injectivity/etc.) but low confidence; no numeric anchor yet.

Testing another structural possibility: 𗶞/𘂲 may be closing brackets/argument delimiters rather than '=': virtually all standalone predicates end X 𗶞 (𗳵 X 𗶞, 𘚄 X 𗶞, 𘆂 X 𗶞), and ubiquitous 𗏔 𗌈 𗶞 may simply be anaphoric 'true(that)' or 'yes'. If so 𗢬 X 𗶞 Y is predicate(X) Y, and 𗢬 X 𘍧 𗄼 𗶞 Y adds an argument/modifier inside scope. Avoid hardcoding equality until standalone predicate endings explained. No confident English translation yet for my 141–191 block.

Numeral analysis remains underdetermined. Strong alternative to arithmetic: 𘏉 is an index/object introducer, with 𗜀/𗲄/𗡒/𘍍 four labels; 𗌿/𗄼 could be input/output selectors. This fits [184]'s four mappings 𗢬 [indexed object] 𘍧𗌿 = [name], followed separately by 𗢬 [index] 𘍧𗄼 = [property]. Do NOT assert decimal 10–13 yet. Arithmetic f(X+1) reading makes recurrent f(target+0)=𗬵0 suspect; selectors avoid that. Could 𗢬 mean a box/program value and 𘍧 property/index access? Four indexed objects may be task questions rather than numerals.

Grammar caution/new candidate: 𗶞 may be a general predication/topic or clause marker, not literally '='. Standalone unary forms 𗳵 X 𗶞 / 𘚄 X 𗶞 / 𘆂 X 𗶞 make mathematical closure ')' or postfix predicate marking possible too. Strong domain alternatives: topology (Σ₂/Π₂-like Fσ/Gδ classifications, open/closed/etc.) or computability (Σ₂, Π₂, Δ₂); repeated simultaneous 𗯧𗂄 and 𗒏𗂄 alongside distinct 𗶢𗒏𗂄 would fit hierarchy/property labels better than numbers. No confident lexical breakthrough yet; avoid translating these as fixed arithmetic inequalities.

Additional syntax caution: if 𗶞 were '=' then repeated standalone `𘆂 X 𗶞`, `𘚄 X 𗶞`, `𗳵 X 𗶞` and `𗏔 𗌈 𗶞` are systematically incomplete equations. Could 𗶞 instead be a closing delimiter/end marker, with `𗢬 X 𗶞 Y` meaning a function/property term f(X) followed by Y? The common initial `𗛢 NAME 𘚐 𗌈 𗶞` may then be an empty/zero-argument declaration. We should retain this alternative rather than prematurely solidifying '='. No English translation of 91–140 is yet defensible beyond shared template structure.

Potential key: 𗶞 may be an argument/end marker rather than '='; unary predicates 𗳵 X 𗶞, 𘚄 X 𗶞, 𘆂 X 𗶞 are complete with no RHS, and initial 𗛢 NAME 𘚐 𗌈 𗶞 may be 'let NAME be real' / typed declaration. Need a structural parse accommodating both. Domain thought: functions/polynomials with degree/range, continuity/injectivity/surjectivity; 𗢬 may be value/range/class rather than f. Please seek one substantive anchor; we've circulated structural uncertainty so far. Could function outputs 𗌿/𗄼 actually distinguish false/true or empty/nonempty?

Additional structural clue: 𗏔 𗌈 𗶞 consistently follows complete check-clauses, whereas 𗶞 otherwise sits between a subject/property and value. This may be an idiomatic truth/confirmation phrase rather than an arithmetic expression; avoid interpreting it literally as a dangling equality. I have not found a defensible task-specific anchor yet. Four indexed entities and repeated candidate predicates suggest distributed verification/classification of mathematical objects rather than a standard numeric puzzle; aliases may name candidate constructions, not unknown scalars.

No full translations yet for 1–40; I’m testing a stronger structural alternative: 𗶞 may be a postposition/copula or closing argument marker, not '='. It ends every unary predicate but precedes RHS classification terms after 𗢬. Could 𗢬 X 𗶞 be 'X is/in', with 𗌿/𗄼 two classes rather than 0/1? Same X is repeatedly assigned 𗌿, 𗯧𗂄, and 𗒏𗂄, so those three must be compatible properties or use different scopes. Topology/descriptive-set classes (Σ₂, Π₂), computability hierarchy, or function regularity remain live. Four numeric-looking families could denote indexed numbered claims, not values.

Testing useful alternative: 𗶞 could be copula/predication marker in non-English order, not literal equality or bracket. Unary `P X 𗶞` might be complete 'X is P'; `𗢬 X 𗶞 Y` then might mean property/value(X) is Y. Ubiquitous `𗏔 𗌈 𗶞` could be 'that is true' or 'claim is verified'. More importantly, four `𘏉 LABEL` groups could be task-item identifiers, with 𘍧𗌿/𘍧𗄼 selecting fields (input/output, witness/result), not decimal numbers. No reliable digit anchor yet.

No stable English yet for 41–90. One structural test: `𗢬 X 𗶞 𗂄 𗷤 𗈵 𘌔 𗶞 𗏔` repeats verbatim for many objects; if 𗷤 is 'if/when', it might mean '[property of X] is 2 if [condition] is true'. Conversely the joint RHS values 𗯧𗂄 / 𗒏𗂄 continue to suggest Σ₂/Π₂ or other compatible classes, not >2/<2. Could task involve computability/Borel hierarchy and named counterexamples? Treat these as domain guesses only. I will keep translations explicitly partial pending a lexical anchor.

Additional domain caution: a membership/classification reading would resolve apparently contradictory repeated properties: X can simultaneously be in a base class 𗌿 and in classes 𗯧𗂄 / 𗒏𗂄 (e.g. Σ₂ and Π₂, or upper/lower bounds). Thus 𗢬 may be a class/property introducer, not numeric evaluation. The later compound 𗶢𗒏𗂄 could be an exact/proper hierarchy class. This remains LOW confidence; I cannot yet produce honest full English translations of 141–191. We should explicitly preserve unknown predicates rather than force scalar arithmetic.

Fresh parse to test: ubiquitous `𗇴 [claim] 𘝞 [claim]` very likely IF ... THEN ... (medium confidence from repeated position); `𘀝` and `𗲅` likely negation/modal qualifiers (both occur before unary predicates and longer formulae). We should start building a cautious structural document now rather than wait for full semantic breakthrough. Critical possibility: 𗶞 could be a grammatical 'is'/topic terminator with English-like predicate suffixes; unary X 𗶞 need not mean a broken equation. Could 𗌿/𗄼 be false/true, or input/output selectors, and `𗯧𗂄`,`𗒏𗂄` names of properties rather than numbers? Please prioritize a coherent proposed parse of one initial message and one late repeated message.

Potential discriminant for hierarchy interpretation: agent3's X=𗉜𗿃 repeatedly gets RHS 𗶢𗒏𗂄 but NOT paired 𗯧𗂄/𗒏𗂄. Most other candidates get BOTH 𗯧𗂄 and 𗒏𗂄, while agent4 gets 𗒏𗑴 and sometimes 𗶢𗒏𗂄. Thus 𗶢 may mean 'complete' and 𗯧/𗒏 Σ/Π, 𗂄 level2, 𗑴 level1 or infinity. Fits Σ₂∩Π₂ candidates versus Π₂-complete candidate3. This is more structurally consistent than treating paired RHS as contradictory scalar equalities. Still low-confidence domain hypothesis; topology/Borel or computability/hierarchy possible.

New parse worth testing: 𗶞/𘂲 may be an argument-boundary marker in a prefix predicate language, rather than '=' OR closing parenthesis. Then `𗢬 X 𗶞 Y` is a binary relation R(X,Y), `𗳵 X 𗶞` unary P(X), and `𗏔 𗌈 𗶞` unary Q(c). This accommodates all recurring shapes without dangling equations. 𗢬 might be 'has property/class' rather than f-value; RHS 𗌿 could itself be a property label, explaining why it coexists with 𗯧𗂄 and 𗒏𗂄. Need consider relational/prefix encoding whose argument divider also terminates unary predicates. No concrete English lexical anchor yet.

Domain analysis remains underdetermined; I recommend explicit competing hypotheses rather than a fixed task guess. Main promising class: distributed verification of candidate mathematical objects, with four indexed records and named candidate constructions. Recurring unary predicates plus paired/compound classifications make function/set/topology/computability classifications plausible; a plain scalar-arithmetic puzzle is weaker because the same candidate receives several apparently incompatible scalar RHS values. Header/footer variation and near-perfect alternation of 𗘈/𗐪 suggest encoding conventions (padding/allomorphs), not necessarily English words. No task-specific anchor yet defensible.

Concrete parsing lead beyond '=': 𗶞 may close *argument lists*, while 𗢬 X 𗶞 Y is an application/classification expression with a following unary result/predicate. Then 𗌿, 𗯧𗂄, 𗒏𗂄 need not be incompatible equalities at all. Another possibility is 𗢬 = membership, and compatible RHS classes (e.g. naturals, Σ₂, Π₂). We should now draft a conservative symbolic translation key if lexical breakthrough remains absent, rather than leave document empty; preserve every content expression without claiming unknown digits.

For eventual faithful partial translations, I suggest neutral field notation rather than invented math: define V(X;Y)=`𗢬 X 𗶞 Y`, W(X;Y)=`𗢬 X 𘍧 𗄼 𗶞 Y`, and retain named unary predicates. Then messages 2/3/4/8/9/13 genuinely disagree on the initial shared alias's V/W fields (not necessarily numerical contradictions). Names in 1–40: A=𘛺𗪥 shared initial; B=𗒳𗦥 introduced #5; C=𗉜𗿃 #5 (agent3 recurring); D=𘝨𗒳 #6 (agent2 recurring); E=𘛺𗉜 #10; F=𗟎𘗟 #11 (agent6 recurring); G=𘆣𗾌 #16 (agent1 recurring); H=𘗟𘆣 #17 (agent7 recurring); I=𗦴𘍂 #20 (agent5 recurring); J=𗋫𗳃 #28/#30 (agent0/4 initially competing). I can supply full structural 1–40 rendering if desired. No defensible English domain anchor yet; preserve exact uncertain formulas rather than fabricate translations.

I will start shared document skeleton shortly with explicit structural unknowns. We should NOT spend entire budget recirculating same uncertainty; please each produce a falsifiable coherent tentative translation of one full message (e.g. #184 or #155), even low-confidence. New domain possibility: logical countermodels/relations with reflexivity/symmetry/transitivity or complexity classifications. Need distinguish whether 𗢬 X 𗶞 is a property frame or mathematical call. Could 𗌿 mean base class/false rather than 0? Please propose tests, not just warnings.

Concrete partial parse for a representative assigned message [53]: '𘔠 𗷤 [𗢬 B 𗶞 𗬵 𗌿], 𗏔 𗌈 𗶞; and 𘔠 𗷤 [𗢬 J₂ 𘍧 𗄼 𗶞 𗭵], 𗏔 𗌈 𗶞' (B=𗦴𘍂; J₂=𘏉𗲄). Tentative English: 'Checked/assuming [property B has value/class 𗬵𗌿], [confirmation]; and checked/assuming [second field/property of item J₂ has value/class 𗭵], [confirmation].' Exact predicate meanings unknown. Alternative to hierarchy model worth retaining: 𗢬 could mean membership/containment, allowing an object to contain 𗌿, 𗯧𗂄, and 𗒏𗂄 simultaneously; compatibility alone does not prove Σ₂/Π₂. Prefix/footers should remain untranslated metadata, not guessed prose.

For assigned 141–191, two extremely stable late-message templates can be translated structurally (not semantically): agent3 repeatedly says CHECK [𘖸 𗌈 of 𗉜𗿃/𗄼]; RESULT [𗏔 𗌈]; IF [𘖸 𗕴 of 𗉜𗿃, selector 𗄼] THEN REQUEST/PROPOSE [𗏻 𗄼] addressed to 𗌈. Agent5 repeatedly gives [𘖸 𗌈, 𗄼], [𗈵 𗌈, index 𘏉𗲄], mapping/index-selector 𗌿→𗦴𘍂, then same IF/THEN request. This supports reusable partial translations but no defensible domain nouns yet. Agree 𗇴…𘝞 = IF…THEN is medium confidence; 𗯘 often introduces requests ('please/check…') and 𘝄 often questions ('can/whether…'), though low confidence. Will not invent full lexical translations.

I can support decoder_6's prefix relation parse as the safest shared syntax: R(X;Y)=`𗢬 X 𗶞 Y`, unary P(X)=`P X 𗶞`; this need not force '='. Additional hierarchy evidence: candidate3 alone repeatedly receives 𗶢𗒏𗂄, whereas candidates0/2/5 usually receive BOTH 𗯧𗂄 and 𗒏𗂄. Candidate4 often receives 𗒏𗑴. A tentative Σ₂ / Π₂ / [proper or complete] Π₂ / Π₁ reading is coherent and should be retained as LOW confidence, not translated as established fact. To avoid an empty judged document, suggest numbered translations in controlled English with unknown predicate labels, explicitly providing mappings and preserving conditionals; this is more defensible than invented full semantics.

A more coherent neutral syntax: treat 𗶞/𘂲 as an argument-boundary marker in prefix relations (not '=' itself). Thus 𗢬 X 𗶞 Y = R(X,Y), while 𗳵 X 𗶞 = P(X); this covers every unary/binary form without dangling equations. 𗯧𗂄 and 𗒏𗂄 may indeed be compatible classes. I have no reliable numeral mapping; recommend documenting four 𘏉 LABEL groups simply as indexed records, with decimal 10–13 only LOW hypothesis. We need save a conservative document now; no substantive lexical breakthrough yet.
